seed.defect: TryParse builds a validated value object without Create, so binding a route, query, header or form value takes a value Create refuses.

seeds.defect: Neither decimal converter narrows the scale: both write a decimal with the scale it arrived with (7.80, 7.8000).
DecimalNumberJsonConverter writes the smallest scale as a string, not as a number.
DecimalStringJsonConverter writes the smallest scale as a number, not as a string.
Both decimal converters refuse a string holding a number.
Both decimal converters narrow the scale of what they read (7.80 reads as 7.8), as a number or a string.
Both decimal converters write a decimal dictionary key with the scale it arrived with, so a key over a decimal, or over a value object over one, keeps its spellings.
AsOptionalText and AsOptionalIdentifier turn a hidden-character string into no text, as a blank one, rather than refusing it as Hidden.
An empty or whitespace-only string passes the guard as empty text; only null is Blank.
AsOptionalText and AsOptionalIdentifier keep Blank a refusal instead of no value.
A null string is Hidden, not Blank.
A composed fault's problem drops the problem type its own set's mapping gives it.
A composed fault's problem drops the occurrence's detail.
A composed fault's operation lists its statuses in descending order.
A status two fault sets share names only the problem types of the first set the endpoint answers with.
The startup check skips an unmapped fault type on an endpoint that answers with several, so the host starts.
WithoutFaults leaves nothing out of the document: an operation still lists the status and problem type of a member its endpoint, group or controller leaves out.
A member the endpoint leaves out is answered with its mapped status instead of throwing an InvalidOperationException.
A group's or a builder's status for a member stops the host as soon as one of its endpoints leaves the member out, though the others keep it.
A status that every endpoint of its scope leaves out no longer stops the host.
WithRule writes a closed set's rule as its member's bare name, without its type's: RuleSet.X is written X.
WithRule names an enum rule without its nesting chain: Rules.Fault.NoAt is written Fault.NoAt.
A fault that names a rule is answered 400, not the status its mapping gives the error.
WithRule takes an enum value no member names, a combination of flags or a cast number, and writes it as a rule.
WithRule names an enum rule with its namespace: PRule.A is written Probes.PRule.A.
FaultKind.Malformed is answered and documented as 422, not 400.
A fault-set member's description is not written as the problem's detail.
A member without a description is given its name as the problem's detail.
AddFaultResponses<TSet>() maps a member of no kind to 500 instead of failing.
AddFaultResponses() answers a member of kind Conflict with 400, not the 409 its kind gives.
AddFaultResponses(fault => ...) keeps only the status its mapping gives and drops the problem type.
A fault set mapped on its own loses its mapping to the mapping for every set (AddFaultResponses()), which is consulted first.
The startup check skips an endpoint that answers with an unmapped enum, so the host starts.
AddFaultResponses() answers a fault-set member of no kind with 500 instead of stopping the start.
AddFaultResponses(fault => ...) answers a member its mapping throws for, or gives a status that is no error, with 500 instead of stopping the start.
Bare fault names are compared as qualified ones, so two fault types an endpoint answers with that write one name (HFault.Clash beside KFault.Clash) log no startup warning.
Qualified fault names are compared with their namespace, so two sets of one nesting chain in two namespaces log no startup warning.
The startup warning names only the first of the two members written alike.
Under QualifiedFaultNames, fault names are still compared bare, so HFault.Clash beside KFault.Clash logs a warning.
The same-name check counts a member the endpoint leaves out, so leaving one out does not end the warning.
The value object implements only its direct base's IEquatable<TBase> again, so a collection of a deeper base compares it by that base's own equality.
Over a base record, the generated Equals(TSelf) also calls the base's Equals(TBase), so a base comparing by reference makes two value objects over one value unequal.
The Preserve guard misses a wrapped class the serializer walks as an object, so a value object over it writes and reads its own $id and $ref instead of refusing.
Under ReferenceHandler.Preserve, the guard refuses a value object over any reference type, a string or a Uri written by a value converter included.
Under ReferenceHandler.Preserve, the guard refuses a value object whose wrapped type the application converts with a converter of its own.
The Preserve guard fires under ReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles too.
A wrapped type whose static Parse returns a type it can't be assigned from is parsed through its type converter, so the value object has parsing.
A wrapped type whose Parse or string constructor takes its text by ref is parsed through its type converter, so the value object has parsing.
An abstract wrapped class with a string constructor is parsed through its type converter, so the value object has parsing.
Only a generated converter's description is read: an application's own IDescribedJsonConverter, the decimal converters among them, leaves its type undescribed.
A description the options give through JsonSchemaDescriptions is never found.
A list's items and a dictionary's additionalProperties of a described type are filled only where ASP.NET already wrote them, so the document drops them.
A query parameter of a described type is described as its converter writes JSON, not as ASP.NET writes it without converters.
Every patch is taken out of required, also a constructor parameter that RespectRequiredConstructorParameters makes the serializer require.
Every patch is listed in required, also one the serializer lets a body leave out.
The default of a Patch<T>, what a field the request leaves out keeps, reads as Null instead of Absent.
A problem response the endpoint declares itself gets no fault or rule on its own schema, only on the shared component.
A problem response the endpoint declares itself keeps ASP.NET's description, which names none of the problem types answered with its status.
An operation's responses are left in the order they were added, so a status the endpoint declares itself comes before the lower fault statuses.
Only an application/problem+json response counts as a declared problem, so [ProducesResponseType<ProblemDetails>(404)] under application/json names no problem types.
The document reads an MVC action's metadata from its descriptor, so what MapControllers()'s builder declares (WithFaultStatus, WithoutFaults) reaches the response but not the document.
The document lists every member, also one the endpoint, its controller or its builder leaves out.
The document lists each member's mapped status, not the one its endpoint, controller or builder sets, which the response answers with.
A type the minimal-API options describe and MVC's options say nothing of is not refused, so the document describes JSON the controllers do not write.
The refusal names the type but not what each set of options says of it.
A type held only inside a patch is never compared across the two option sets, so the document describes it as the minimal-API options alone say.
Two option sets with the same converters are refused when their naming policy or number handling differs.
A host of minimal APIs alone is compared against MVC's default options, so a converter on its own options refuses its document.
CMTK0014 no longer judges a conversion, so a cast to a FaultKind or a ConstructorAccessibility that names no member is silent.
CMTK0014 takes a zero for a member, so default, default(FaultKind) and (FaultKind)0 are silent.
CMTK0014 no longer reads ConstructorAccessibility, so RequireParameterlessConstructor's argument that names no member is silent.
CMTK0014 is reported at the syntax around the value, not at the value.
CMTK1023 leaves out a base's explicit IEquatable<TBase>.Equals, so a base comparing by reference through it compiles without a word.
CMTK1023 is reported as information, not as a warning.
Over a base record, the generated GetHashCode() combines the base's, so a base hashing by reference makes two value objects over one value hash apart.
CMTK0010 no longer checks a collection expression's builder method, so a breaking argument it infers there compiles.
CMTK0010 takes a sealed class for [Unsealed].
CMTK0010 takes any type that is not an interface for [ValueObject], value object or not.
CMTK0010 takes a mutable struct for [ReadOnlyStruct].
CMTK0010 reports a breach of [Distinct] or [Unrelated] at the earlier argument of the pair.
ShouldHold(reason) checks only the held fault's type, so a fault of that type with another reason passes.
ShouldHold(reason) never finds a reason of a composed fault's last type: it reads that case as the bare reason, not as a Fault<TFault>.
ShouldHold(reason) hands back a new Fault<TFault> of the reason alone, without the held fault's detail and rule.
ShouldHold(reason) reads an uninitialized composed fault instead of failing as an assertion.
A failed ShouldHold(reason) no longer says which fault the composed fault holds.
A value object's OpenAPI schema drops the wrapped type's format (int32, uuid, date-time).

6866822 reversed: a nullable value object admits null where ASP.NET's exporter puts none for the wrapped type (a query, header or form VO?, a nullable struct over string or Uri at a root), and an MVC [FromBody] VO? none where the wrapped ulong? or long? has one.
A list's or an array's items are not put back for a container of value objects, so the elements lose their schema.
A dictionary keyed by a value object is described with the key's schema for its values.
Under OpenAPI 2.0 and 3.0 a value object's schema drops the wrapped type's format.
CMTK1005's message no longer ends with the link to the Build errors table.
A record class not declared sealed is no longer refused (CMTK1006 is never reported).
The fabric hands the aspect no wrapped-value-object refusal, so a value object over another value object is generated.
A generic wrapped type is no longer refused, so List<T> fails inside the generated code (LAMA0611) instead of CMTK1005.
1ef30be reversed: the fabric no longer reports CMTK1022, so an abstract type with a marker compiles with nothing generated and nothing said.
e4b751c's System.Enum refusal reversed: a value object over System.Enum is no longer refused (CMTK1005).
e4b751c's name refusal reversed: a value object named From, Parse, MinValue or another generated member is not refused, and fails inside the generated code (LAMA0611, CS0542).
e4b751c's set-name refusal reversed: a closed set named Name, All, Match or another of its generated members is not refused (CMTK1021) and fails inside the generated code.
e4b751c's operator refusal reversed: a hand-written operator == or != between two of the type is C#'s bare CS0111, with no CMTK1011 naming it.
CMTK1005 is reported as a warning, so a declaration that cannot be generated builds, with nothing generated for it.
53188ed reversed: a value object over object is no longer refused (CMTK1005) and compiles.
A value object over an enum is mapped as a text column, as a closed set is, not as the enum's integer column.
A convention marks every value-object property required, so a nullable one gets a NOT NULL column.
A finalizing convention clears the maximum length, precision, scale and column type configured on a value-object property.
The member translator leaves .Value to EF, so a filter, sort or grouping on it is not translated.
The method-call translator leaves GetValue() to EF, so a query on it is not translated.
The method-call translator leaves ValueOrNull() to EF, so a query on an optional value object's value is not translated.
.Value on a column is translated as a cast of the column, not the column itself.
A decimal value object is mapped through the double mapping, a REAL column, not the TEXT column a decimal gets.
The type mapping plugin maps no value object used as a key or an index, so a value-object key cannot be stored.
A convention marks every value-object property required, so a nullable one cannot store null.
A key over an integer is declared never generated, so entities added without a key are stored with 0.
A key over byte is declared generated on add, which EF does not do for a plain byte key.
A key over char is declared generated on add, as EF would for a plain char key.
A key over a Guid is declared generated on add, so EF invents a Guid for an entity added without one.
A query comparing a value object with a hand-written CompareTo (an operator or CompareTo) runs in the database instead of throwing.
A query ordering by a value object with a hand-written CompareTo runs in the database instead of throwing.
Min or Max of a value object with a hand-written CompareTo runs in the database instead of throwing.
An equality of a value object with a hand-written CompareTo is refused as if it were a comparison.
Ordering by .Value of a value object with a hand-written CompareTo is refused as if it ordered by the value object.
A query filter comparing a value object with a hand-written CompareTo is accepted when the model is built.
.Value translates on a column the application converts itself, so the query compares against the converted text instead of failing.
The query interceptor rewrites a value-object equality as an equality of .Value, which a column the application converts itself cannot answer.
A closed set's member is stored as its name in upper case, not its name.
The JSON reader/writer of a closed set writes something other than the member's name, so a primitive collection or a JSON column holds no names.
A stored name the closed set no longer has reads back as null instead of throwing.
An instance that is not a member of its closed set is written as the name Unknown instead of throwing.
TypeKit's conventions ignore an Option or Result property, so the model builds without the column instead of failing.
The type mapping plugin refuses an Option or Result property with an error that does not name the type.
FirstOrNoneAsync with a condition reads every matching row, without LIMIT 1.
SingleOrNoneAsync answers the first of two matching rows instead of throwing.
ElementAtOrNone on a query reads every row up to its index and skips in memory, without OFFSET.
Reading a column back runs Create and throws for a value today's rules refuse, instead of materializing it.
The generated Revalidate() answers the value object itself, so a stored value today's rules refuse reads as valid.
UseTypeKit() adds its services only when the provider's are already registered, so calling it before UseSqlite does nothing.
A finalizing convention clears the max length, precision and scale of value-object properties, so a convention on the value object's type does not reach its property.
.Value on an element of a primitive collection of value objects is not translated, so Any(t => t.Value == x) fails.
The integer key of a TPH or TPT hierarchy's root is left as EF leaves a value object, never generated.
Under TPC on a provider without a sequence (SQLite), an integer key of the hierarchy's root stays generated on add.
The first value-object property of a composite key is treated as a single integer key and generated on add.
The integer key default is set as an explicit configuration, so it overrides the application's own ValueGeneratedNever.
A key over char or Guid is declared never generated as an explicit configuration, so it overrides the application's own ValueGeneratedOnAdd.
A finalizing convention clears the column type configured on a value-object property.
A finalizing convention removes the converter the application configured on a value-object property, so TypeKit's mapping stores the plain value.
A finalizing convention makes a value-object property required again after the application configured IsRequired(false).
A dictionary key is written with ToString(), not the wrapped type's key converter and DictionaryKeyPolicy.
The generated converter writes a number as it is, ignoring the options' JsonNumberHandling.WriteAsString.
The generated converter refuses a JSON string that holds an escape sequence, which the wrapped type reads.
Generated parsing calls the wrapped type's Parse instead of its TryParse, whose FormatException quotes the input.
A JSON value the wrapped type can't read is refused with its text in the JsonException's message.
Generated parsing refuses unreadable text with an inner FormatException that quotes it.
Parse and the type converter build a validated value object without Create.
TryFrom wraps the value without Create, so it gives a value Create refuses.
The JSON converter's materialize flag is read backwards: a JSON read skips Create, and only StoredJsonConverterFactory runs it.
The JsonException, the FormatException and the FromKnownGood exception name the type of the fault Create returned, not the fault.
Generated formatting uses the current culture instead of the provider (invariant by default).
The type converter writes the wrapped value in the current culture when no culture is passed.
The type converter reads text in the current culture when no culture is passed.
The generated converter lets the wrapped converter's own exception out for input it can't read (a FormatException for a Guid).
A deeper base record whose IEquatable is implemented explicitly keeps its own Equals, so equal value objects compare unequal through that base and a HashSet of it holds both.
Over a base record, the generated GetHashCode() hashes the value's text, so 7.8m and 7.80m, or 0.0 and -0.0, hash apart.
The generated CompareTo orders the wrapped values in reverse.
The refusing converter writes {} for an Option or a Result instead of throwing NotSupportedException, so a Some is written as {} and reads back as None.
Reading an Option or a Result throws a JsonException, as for malformed input, not NotSupportedException.
